# MarketsOnDeck

> Real trades, graded in public, before the outcome is known — wins and losses both. MarketsOnDeck is run by one person (Keith) documenting his own real brokerage account: every episode and every Morning Brief carries a full investment disclaimer (not advice, not a recommendation, past results don't predict future ones) and an affiliate disclosure. The differentiator from typical trading content is verifiability — numbers are cross-checked against the source trade journal, discrepancies are disclosed rather than hidden, and losses get exactly as much airtime as wins.

## Episodes
- [Episode 1: The Baseline](/episodes/01-the-baseline.html): July 14-31, 2026 — eighteen days, every closed trade, net +$2,960.50, including a real losing day (July 17) shown with the same weight as the wins.
- [Episode 2: The August Swing](/episodes/02-the-august-swing.html): August 1-20, 2026 — the same ticker (SOXL) produced the largest win (+$1,930) and largest loss (-$1,492) of the period hours apart, revealed to be two legs of one put credit spread. Net +$5,688.52.

## Daily
- [Morning Brief](/brief/index.html): Short daily market notes tied to the site owner's real positions, archived like a blog.
